title: Reconcile asymmetric shard merge causing ghost usage in per-model charts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We are observing intermittent "ghost" token/req counts in per-model Console charts and per-customer breakdowns: short-lived spikes that do not correlate with request logs or backend ingress metrics. These anomalies appear to coincide with shard merge windows when the streaming-rate-limiter aggregates sharded tallies.

Observed behavior and scope:
- Symptom: 1–5 minute spikes in per-model token counts that later partially vanish after backfill reconciliation; sometimes there are compensating undercounts in later buckets.
- Affected surfaces: Console timeseries charts, per-model cost breakdown, and quota consumption estimation for a subset (~0.4%) of customers across multiple regions.
- Time window: First reported 2026-02-24; reproduced in dev with a sharded ingest simulator.
- Impact: Billing confidence degraded (medium). Alerts are firing for downstream quota thresholds in noisy accounts.

Investigation notes & hypothesis:
- Root cause hypothesis: asymmetric shard fan-in during high-ingest/partition-rebalance causes duplicate-accept of late-arriving partial tallies because the idempotency marker (ingest_seq+shard_epoch) is not canonicalized consistently across the sharded aggregator and the rollback/backfill dedup path. When the merge completes, some partial tallies are applied twice to the rolling window until retroactive reconciliation runs.
- Evidence:
  - Correlation between spikes and shard-merge logs in ingress service (merge_event IDs present).
  - Development replay showed race where aggregator A accepts delta X with seq S and aggregator B also accepts same delta when leadership changed; the dedupe table uses a TTL that expired before the final commit in rare cases.
  - Backfill job (retro-recon service) subsequently emits compensating negative deltas but only to global totals; per-model per-customer series use a different aggregation path and missed the compensation in some bucket alignments.

Immediate mitigation options (short-lived):
- Increase dedupe TTL on shard-aggregator to cover the worst-case merge window (fast mitigation, low-risk) — risk: larger dedupe state memory cost.
- Temporarily disable auto-merge/fast-rebalance for high-ingest tenants while we deploy a long-term fix (operational, requires SRE coordination).

Proposed long-term fix (preferred):
1) Canonicalize ingest idempotency token at the routing layer (ingress) before sharding so that duplicates surface identical canonical keys across shards.
2) Extend reconciliation path: ensure retro-recon emits per-model per-customer compensating deltas along the same aggregation pipeline used by Console timeseries (remove current path divergence).
3) Add deterministic bucket attribution for late events (use event_time floor + source_offset) so that compensations land in the same bucket boundaries.
4) Add an explicit post-backfill verification pass that computes model-level totals and reconciles client-visible series, surfaced as an operator job with a dry-run mode.

Design for rollout and validation:
- Phase 0 (now): Increase dedupe TTL to 10m for shard-aggregators in canary regions (eu-west-1). Rollout window 30m, monitor.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement canonicalization at ingress and unit tests for canonical token collision coverage. Canary rollout to staging, then prod-nightly to a small tenant cohort.
- Phase 2 (3–4 weeks): Change retro-recon to write compensating deltas through the primary aggregation stream; add bucket-determinism.
- Phase 3: Run operator verification pass across 7 days of rolling windows to validate no residual drift; mark as done and reduce dedupe TTL back to baseline if safe.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Eliminate unexplained per-model spikes (>95% reduction in incidents) across sampled tenants for 72h post-rollout.
- Retro-recon compensations shown in Console series (visible in the same bucket boundaries) and automated reconciliation job reports zero net drift for 7 days.
- No increase in false quota triggers for affected customers.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalization and dedupe TTL logic.
- Integration: sharded ingest simulator that replays leadership handoffs and out-of-order deltas; assert final aggregate equals single-shard ground truth.
- Staging canary with real traffic subset; create synthetic traffic that previously produced ghost spikes and assert no spikes after fix.

Required changes & owners:
- ingress: canonical token generation (owner: Ethan Cole)
- shard-aggregator: dedupe TTL bump + logs (owner: Priya Singh)
- retro-recon: emit per-model compensations via aggregation bus (owner: Miguel Herrera)
- console: acceptance test dashboards and verification job (owner: Lina Zhao)

Rollout notes and monitoring:
- Dashboards to watch: per-model token delta heatmap, aggregation-lag histogram, dedupe-hit-rate, retro-recon-compensations (new).
- Alerts: increase threshold for unexplained spikes to avoid alert fatigue; add an alert when retro-recon backlog > 15m.

Backfill / migration plan:
- Run retro-recon in dry-run across last 30 days to estimate compensation volume.
- If compensation is moderate (<0.5% of tokens), apply compensations directly; otherwise, schedule staged compensation windows per-customer to avoid billing surprises and communicate to affected customers.

Open questions & risks:
- Memory impact of longer dedupe TTL on aggregator (SRE to approve).
- Edge case where event_time is extremely late (customer replay) — ensure compensations do not exceed retention windows.
- Communication plan for billing-sensitive customers if we apply retroactive compensations to billed amounts.
